title: Degraded interconnect: staggered GPU evacuation & replacement playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft runbook for partial GPU visibility or degraded PCIe/interconnect on nodes (examples: intermittent NVLink/PCIe flaps, root complex errors, partial device list). The focus here is on a staggered evacuation and hardware replacement process that minimizes disruption and avoids mass drain-induced capacity collapse.

Scope:
- Applies to racks/nodes with 1+ GPUs that become partially visible or intermittently fail health checks
- Covers on-call triage, safe cordon/drain patterns, temporary capacity bridges, cold/hot GPU carrier swaps, firmware/BIOS patch path, and backfill capacity plan
- Not a substitute for full datacenter hardware SOPs (for physical rack work use hardware team checklist)

Signals that should trigger this playbook:
- Node health probes show GPU count mismatch vs inventory (e.g., 8 -> 5 visible)
- dmesg/host kernel shows AER/PCIe root complex errors
- Prometheus alert: gpu_device_pods_failed_count rising or kubelet-device-plugin flapping
- NVLink error counters above baseline or ECC/dma errors surging

First 10 minutes (Triage):
- Post to #sre-oncall + @infra-hardware with short summary (node, zone, alert, impact):
  - example: "Interconnect flap: node gpu-r3-12 showing 3/8 GPUs visible, traffic requeued, 6k pending tokens — starting containment"
- Check node status: kubectl get nodes -o wide; confirm Pod distribution
- Run quick diagnostics (as SRE):
  - ssh root@node -> dmesg | tail -n 200 -> capture AER/PCIe faults
  - nvidia-smi -q -> check driver errors, pid collisions, stale processes
  - lspci -vv | grep -A3 NVIDIA -> check bus visibility
- Capture logs and attach to incident ticket (JIRA JIRA-SRV-8811 or new ticket)

Containment (30 minutes):
Goal: stop error amplification, avoid mass drains.
- If node shows flapping and pods are failing, mark node unschedulable (cordon) but DO NOT drain all pods immediately.
  - kubectl cordon <node>
- For essential low-latency pods that tolerate eviction, evict selectively from the most-impacted GPUs only: use device plugin labels to target pods bound to failing GPU indices, or use annotation-based eviction helper.
- If device plugin cannot target indices, prioritize draining stateless/replicated workloads first (worker pools, batch jobs). Leave long-running pinned workloads where possible.
- If errors are causing OOMs or host instability, escalate to full drain and move forward with replacement.

Staggered evacuation pattern (why):
- Draining all pods from one node at once can trigger cluster-wide scheduling pressure and cascade into other nodes (esp. small clusters or reserved-capacity tenants).
- We do a 2-phase evacuation:
  1) Selective drain: evict pods on failing GPU indices (hotspots) and allow scheduler to rescale gradually.
  2) If health does not improve within cooldown window (15–30m), perform full drain and replace hardware while using capacity-bridge nodes.

Capacity-bridge options (to avoid service disruption):
- Warm spare nodes (preferred): Identify pre-warmed spare nodes in same AZ/zone and move traffic there. List at-hand: spare-* pools in Dedicated.
- Cross-zone spill: If latency budget allows, schedule evicted pods to cross-zone pools temporarily. Update routing policy if necessary.
- Temporary burst VMs: Launch small number of on-demand GPU instances and attach to pool with placement constraints. (Owner: platform-eng)

Hardware replacement (physical/field steps, operator notes):
- Determine replacement type:
  - Hotplug-capable GPU carrier: can attempt GPU reseat without power cycle (follow vendor guide)
  - Cold-swap: require node powercycle and data center approval
- Coordinate with on-site hardware team and schedule a maintenance window if cold-swap required. Post in slack #infra-hardware and incident channel.
- Pre-replacement checklist:
  - Confirm backups for any local ephemeral volumes (scratch) used by long-running pods
  - Note node serial, chassis ID, PCIe slot, GPU carrier ID
  - Ensure spare parts available (carrier, retainer bracket, thermal paste if applicable)
  - Confirm BMC/iLO access for remote power control
- Replacement steps (hot-resettle attempt first):
  1) Stop workloads touching the failing GPU index (selective eviction) and wait 2–3 min
  2) Run vendor hot-swap script (if available) to unbind device from kernel and rebind after reseat
  3) Reseat GPU in carrier, verify PCIe link speed and visibility (lspci + nvidia-smi)
  4) If device returns healthy, uncordon node and reconcile pod placement slowly
  5) If device still failing, schedule cold swap per vendor SOP

Cold swap and node powercycle (if required):
- Notify impacted teams and set incident running state to maintenance
- Power down node via BMC, perform physical replacement, power on
- Run full diagnostics: nvml tests, stress small load (e.g., small inference job) for 5–10 minutes before returning to service
- Bring node back to cluster: kubelet should report all GPUs; run kubelet-device-plugin restart if necessary

Post-replace verification (before full traffic):
- GPU visibility: nvidia-smi -L shows N devices expected
- Kernel logs: no new AER/PCIe errors in last 5 minutes
- Run smoke inference test against pinned model (use canary model route) — latency within baseline
- Run 1–2 job reschedules to confirm scheduler behavior
- Monitor for 60m; if stable, uncordon and let scheduler backfill incrementally

Cluster recovery and backfill (after node healthy):
- Gradual uncordon: uncordon and monitor for surges in scheduling. If backlog is large, increase max-surge/concurrency limits in small steps.
- Use rate-limited backfill script (link: CONFLUENCE-1234/backfill-scripts) to avoid overwhelming control plane
- If capacity is insufficient, trigger capacity-add runbook (see: capacity-add quick path below)

Capacity-add quick path (when replacement will take >2 hours or multiple nodes affected):
- Contact platform-eng on-call to spin up pre-approved burst pool (tag: gpu-burst)
- Schedule tenant-aware migrations (avoid GDPR/Private VPC migrations without approvals)
- Use autoscaler override to temporarily raise desired counts for stateful sets that support it; roll back after normalized

Incident after-actions (short list for SRE owner):
- Collect logs, timeline, and attach to ticket
- Run quick RCA template (who, what, when, why, immediate fix, long-term mitigation) and link to incident
- Identify if firmware/driver update is required across fleet: open CHORE in runtime team with affected node list
- Add proactive check to node health exporter (new metric?): pci_link_error_rate or nvlink_error_count alert threshold

Known gotchas and heuristics (notes-to-self):
- Do NOT mass-reboot nodes in same rack; thermal/cold-start spikes may trip PSU or PDU circuits
- On shared racks, replacing multiple GPUs simultaneously can cause power distribution issues — stagger replacements across PDUs
- Some workloads pin GPUs by index; eviction could fail silently if operator uses wrong annotation. Double-check pod device-mapping with `kubectl describe pod`
- Driver reload often masks hardware issue; prefer physical verification before fleet-wide driver rollouts

Runbook TODOs and follow-ups (in this doc):
- [ ] Add exact vendor hot-swap scripts for A100/H100 carriers (platform-eng)
- [ ] Link exact spare-node list and escalation contacts for each region
- [ ] Create a small automated selective-evict helper CLI (sre-tooling ticket)
- [ ] Add preflight BMC access checklist for on-call rotation

Who to ping (short):
- #sre-oncall (first responder)
- #infra-hardware (hardware operations)
- @platform-eng-oncall (capacity/burst)
- @runtime-team (driver/bug investigation)

Example quick note to post in incident channel (copy-paste):
"Interconnect degradation detected on gpu-r3-12 (3/8 GPUs visible). Cordoned node, selectively evicting impacted pods (phase 1). Running device reseat/hotplug. If not resolved in 30m, will schedule cold swap and request spare node bridge. Ticket: JIRA-SRV-8811."

Revision history:
- 2025-11-18: initial draft (Priya)
- 2026-02-20: added capacity-bridge pattern and cold-swap checklist (Miguel)

End of draft.
